**Paid Sick Leave Policy – California & New York** *Effective Date:* [Insert Date] *Policy Reference Number:* PSL‑2026‑01 --- ### 1. Purpose This policy establishes the minimum paid sick leave that **[Company Name]** must provide to employees working in California and New York, in accordance with each state’s statutory requirements. It is designed to be a single written document that satisfies both jurisdictions without granting more leave than required. > *Note:* The company already offers 10 days of general Paid Time Off (PTO). Sick leave under this policy is **separate** from PTO and may not be used for non‑sick‑leave purposes unless otherwise specified by law. --- ### 2. Eligibility All full‑time, part‑time, and temporary employees who work **≥ 20 hours per week** in California or New York are eligible. Employees who work less than 20 hours per week accrue sick leave on a pro‑rated basis (see §3). > *Assumption:* “Full‑time” is defined as ≥ 30 hours/week; “part‑time” < 30 but ≥ 20. --- ### 3. Accrual | State | Minimum Annual Accrual | Accrual Rate | Cap on Accrued Hours | |-------|------------------------|--------------|----------------------| | **California** | 24 hours (3 days) | 1 hour per 30 worked hours | **24 hours** | | **New York** | 40 hours (5 days) | 1 hour per 30 worked hours | **40 hours** | #### 3.1 California Employees - Accrue at **1 hour for every 30 hours worked**. - Maximum accrual is capped at **24 hours** per calendar year; any additional hours earned beyond this cap are not accrued (i.e., no “extra” sick leave). - Unused hours may be carried over to the next calendar year. The company may allow unlimited carryover, but it will never exceed the statutory minimum. #### 3.2 New York Employees - Accrue at **1 hour for every 30 hours worked**. - Maximum accrual is capped at **40 hours** per calendar year; any additional hours earned beyond this cap are not accrued. - Unused hours may be carried over indefinitely, subject to the same cap. > *Clarification:* The policy does **not** provide more than the statutory minimum in either jurisdiction. Employees in California will never accrue more than 24 hours; employees in New York will never accrue more than 40 hours. --- ### 4. Use of Sick Leave | State | Eligible Reasons for Use | |-------|--------------------------| | **California** | • Employee’s own illness, injury or medical appointment
• Family member (spouse, child, parent, grandparent, sibling) illness/injury/medical appointment
• Preventive care
• Domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking situations | | **New York** | • Employee’s own illness, injury or medical appointment
• Family member (spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, grandparent, sibling) illness/injury or medical appointment
• Preventive care | - Sick leave may be taken in **any increment of 1 hour**. - Employees must provide reasonable notice and documentation when possible. Documentation is required for any sick‑leave period that exceeds **3 consecutive days** (72 hours). --- ### 5. Request & Documentation Process 1. **Notice:** Employees should notify their supervisor as soon as practicable, but no later than the start of the shift. 2. **Documentation:** - For absences ≤ 3 days: written statement from employee is sufficient. - For absences > 3 days: a medical certificate or other documentation (e.g., doctor’s note) must be submitted within 5 business days of return to work. 3. **Recordkeeping:** Supervisors will record sick‑leave usage in the company’s HR system and ensure accrual balances are updated promptly. --- ### 6. Carryover & Expiration | State | Carryover Policy | |-------|------------------| | **California** | Unused hours may be carried over to the next calendar year; no expiration. | | **New York** | Unused hours may be carried over indefinitely; no expiration. | > *Assumption:* The company will not impose a separate cap on carryover beyond the statutory maximums listed in §3. --- ### 7. Interaction with PTO - Sick leave under this policy is **not** interchangeable with general PTO unless an employee’s state law explicitly allows it (California does not allow substitution; New York permits but only if the employer has a written policy that meets statutory requirements). - Employees may use PTO for any purpose, including sick‑leave reasons, but doing so will **reduce** their available paid sick leave under this policy. --- ### 8. Compliance & Updates - This policy is compliant with the California Healthy Workplaces, Healthy Families Act (HWHA) and the New York Paid Sick Leave Law (PSLL). - The company will review state statutes annually and update this policy if laws change. Employees will be notified of any material changes within 30 days. --- ### 9. Policy Review | Reviewer | Frequency | |----------|-----------| | HR Manager | Annually | | Legal Counsel | As needed (e.g., after statutory amendments) | --- **By signing below, the employee acknowledges receipt and understanding of this Paid Sick Leave Policy.** Employee Signature: ________________________ Date: __________ HR Representative: _________________________ Date: __________ --- *This policy satisfies both California’s 24‑hour minimum and New York’s 40‑hour minimum without granting any employee more leave than required by law.*
